ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the pentagon $ABCDE$, $AB \perp BC$, $AE \perp DE$, $AB=1$, $BC=2$, $CD=2\sqrt{5}$, $DE=3$, $AE=4$. Find the area of the pentagon $ABCDE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $AC$ and $AD$,\\
since $AB\perp BC$ and $AE\perp DE$,\\
thus $\angle B=90^\circ$ and $\angle E=90^\circ$,\\
hence $AB^2+BC^2=AC^2$ and $AE^2+DE^2=AD^2$,\\
since $AB=1$, $BC=2$, $DE=3$, $AE=4$,\\
thus $1^2+2^2=AC^2$ and $4^2+3^2=AD^2$,\\
therefore $AC=\sqrt{5}$ and $AD=5$,\\
since $CD=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
thus $AC^2+CD^2=AD^2$,\\
thus $\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
thus the area of pentagon $ABCDE$ $=S_{\triangle ABC}+S_{\triangle ADE}+S_{\triangle ACD}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC+\frac{1}{2}\cdot AE\cdot DE+\frac{1}{2}\cdot AC\cdot CD$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\times 1\times 2+\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 3+\frac{1}{2}\times \sqrt{5}\times 2\sqrt{5}=1+6+5=\boxed{12}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the pentagon $ABCDE$, $AB \perp BC$, $AE \perp DE$, $AB=1$, $BC=2$, $CD=2\sqrt{5}$, $DE=3$, $AE=4$. Find the area of the pentagon $ABCDE$.
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $AC$ and $AD$,\\
since $AB\perp BC$ and $AE\perp DE$,\\
thus $\angle B=90^\circ$ and $\angle E=90^\circ$,\\
hence $AB^2+BC^2=AC^2$ and $AE^2+DE^2=AD^2$,\\
since $AB=1$, $BC=2$, $DE=3$, $AE=4$,\\
thus $1^2+2^2=AC^2$ and $4^2+3^2=AD^2$,\\
therefore $AC=\sqrt{5}$ and $AD=5$,\\
since $CD=2\sqrt{5}$,\\
thus $AC^2+CD^2=AD^2$,\\
thus $\angle ACD=90^\circ$,\\
thus the area of pentagon $ABCDE$ $=S_{\triangle ABC}+S_{\triangle ADE}+S_{\triangle ACD}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC+\frac{1}{2}\cdot AE\cdot DE+\frac{1}{2}\cdot AC\cdot CD$\\
$=\frac{1}{2}\times 1\times 2+\frac{1}{2}\times 4\times 3+\frac{1}{2}\times \sqrt{5}\times 2\sqrt{5}=1+6+5=\boxed{12}$
